title: Sarma (cabbage rolls)
description: Sour cabbage leaves rolled around rice and minced meat, slowly simmered with smoked ribs. Even better on day two.
steps: Rinse the cabbage leaves in cold water if they taste very sour, and cut out the thick part of each stem.
Fry the chopped onion and half the bacon in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes. Mix with the minced meat, rice, egg, crushed garlic, paprika and pepper.
Put a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Line a large pot with chopped cabbage, layer the rolls with the ribs and the rest of the bacon, add the bay leaves and cover with water.
Simmer gently with the lid on for 2 hours. Do not stir; shake the pot now and then.
Fry the flour in the remaining oil until golden, stir in the paprika and tomato paste with a ladle of cooking water, and pour it over the rolls. Simmer 15 more minutes.

title: Pašticada with gnocchi
description: Dalmatian beef braised for hours in red wine with prunes and vegetables until the sauce is dark, glossy and sweet-sour.

ingredients.note: one piece of topside or silverside

steps: Make small cuts in the beef and push in thin strips of bacon and slices of garlic. Rub with the vinegar, salt and pepper.
Brown the meat on all sides in the oil in a heavy pot, then take it out.
Fry the chopped onion, carrot and celeriac for 10 minutes. Add the tomato paste, cloves, nutmeg, bay leaves and prunes.
Put the meat back, pour in the wine and enough water to half cover it. Cover and simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, turning the meat now and then.
Take out the meat and bay leaves, blend the sauce until smooth and simmer until thick. Slice the meat and warm it in the sauce.
Cook the gnocchi in salted water and serve with the meat and plenty of sauce.

title: Grah (bean stew with smoked meat)
description: A thick, warming bean stew with smoked ribs, paprika and bay. A classic Thursday lunch in Croatian homes.
steps: Soak the beans overnight. Drain, cover with fresh water and bring to the boil, then pour that water away.
Cover the beans and ribs with 2.5 litres of water, add the bay leaves and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the diced carrot and half the onion and cook for 40 more minutes, until the beans are soft.
Fry the rest of the onion in the oil, stir in the flour until golden, then the garlic, paprika and tomato paste. Stir this into the stew.
Simmer 10 minutes, season with pepper (the ribs bring the salt) and serve with bread.

title: Istrian maneštra
description: Hearty Istrian soup of beans, sweetcorn and potato with a little smoked meat, finished with good olive oil.
steps: Simmer the soaked beans with the ribs and bay leaves in 2.5 litres of water for 50 minutes.
Add the diced potato, carrot and celeriac and cook for 25 minutes.
Chop the bacon, garlic and parsley very finely together into a paste (pešt) and fry it with the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes.
Stir the pešt and the drained sweetcorn into the soup and simmer for 10 minutes.
Take out the ribs, cut the meat off the bones and return it. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Fiš paprikaš
description: Slavonian fisherman's stew, red with sweet and hot paprika. Made here with white fish fillets and served with noodles.
steps: Slice the onions thinly and soften them in the oil with a splash of water for 15 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, chili and tomato paste, then the wine and 1 litre of water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the fish in large pieces and the salt. Simmer gently for 10 minutes without stirring, just shake the pot.
Meanwhile cook the noodles. Serve the stew over the noodles.

title: Čobanac (shepherd's stew)
description: Slavonian mixed-meat stew with lots of onion and paprika, simmered until the meat falls apart.
steps: Cut the meat into 3 cm cubes. Brown it in the lard in batches and set aside.
Fry the chopped onions slowly for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, paprika, chili and tomato paste, then the meat, wine, bay leaves, salt and 1.5 litres of water.
Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours. Add the sliced carrot, pepper and potato and cook for 40 more minutes.
The stew should be thick; add a little water if needed. Serve with bread.

title: Stuffed peppers in tomato sauce
description: Peppers filled with rice and minced meat, baked slowly in a light tomato sauce. Served with mashed potato.
steps: Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds.
Mix the meat, rice, chopped onion, egg, paprika, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Fill the peppers loosely (the rice swells).
Stand them in a pot, pour over the passata with 300 ml water and the sugar, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Boil the potatoes, mash with the milk, butter and a pinch of salt, and serve with the peppers and sauce.

title: Grilled sea bream with Swiss chard and potatoes
description: The Dalmatian plate: whole grilled fish with blitva, potatoes, garlic and plenty of olive oil.
steps: Peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 10 minutes. Add the chopped chard and cook 8 more minutes, then drain.
Warm 3 tbsp oil with the sliced garlic, add the potatoes and chard and crush them lightly with a fork. Season with salt.
Brush the cleaned fish with oil, season inside and out and grill or roast at 220 °C for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once.
Serve the fish with the chard and potatoes and a squeeze of lemon.

title: Brudet with polenta
description: Fish stew from the coast, cooked gently in tomato, wine and a little vinegar, with soft polenta on the side.
steps: Soften the sliced onions in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and the squid cut into rings and cook 10 minutes.
Add the passata, wine, vinegar, salt, pepper and 200 ml water. Simmer 10 minutes.
Lay the fish pieces in the sauce, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes. Shake the pot instead of stirring.
Meanwhile stir the polenta into 1 litre of boiling salted water and cook as the packet says.
Scatter the brudet with parsley and serve with the polenta.

title: Mussels buzara
description: Mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic and parsley with breadcrumbs to thicken. Bread for dipping is a must.
steps: Scrub the mussels and pull off the beards. Throw away any that stay open when tapped.
Warm the oil with the chopped garlic in a large pot for 1 minute, add the mussels and wine, cover and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, shaking the pot.
Throw away any mussels that did not open. Stir in the parsley, pepper and breadcrumbs and cook 2 more minutes until the juices thicken.
Serve straight from the pot with bread.

title: Prawn risotto
description: Creamy coastal risotto with prawns, a splash of white wine and lots of parsley.
steps: Dissolve the stock cube in 1.2 litres of hot water and keep it warm.
Soften the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away. Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 3 to 4 minutes until pink. Stir in the butter, parsley and a squeeze of lemon, cover and rest 2 minutes.

title: Ričet (barley and bean stew)
description: Old-fashioned continental stew of pearl barley, beans and smoked meat. Cheap, filling and freezes well.
steps: Simmer the beans, barley, ribs and bay leaves in 2.5 litres of water for 1 hour.
Add the diced carrot, parsnip and potato and cook 30 minutes more.
Fry the onion and garlic in the oil and stir them in. Take the meat off the bones, return it and add the parsley.
Season with pepper and salt only if needed; smoked meat is salty.

title: Savoy cabbage stew with sausage
description: Kelj, potatoes and smoked sausage in one pot, thickened the old way with a little fried flour and garlic.
steps: Shred the kelj, dice the potatoes and cook both in 1.2 litres of water with the Vegeta for 25 minutes.
Slice the sausage and brown it in a dry pan, then add it to the pot.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil, stir in the flour until golden, then the garlic and paprika. Stir into the stew.
Simmer 5 minutes, season with pepper and serve.

title: Breaded chicken with potato salad
description: Crisp breaded chicken fillets with a Slavonian-style warm potato salad dressed with oil, vinegar and onion.

ingredients.note: for frying, some stays in the pan

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes. Peel while warm and slice.
Dress the potatoes with the thinly sliced onion, vinegar, 3 tbsp of the frying oil (or the pumpkin seed oil), salt and pepper.
Slice the chicken into thin escalopes, season, then coat in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes a side until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper.
Serve with the potato salad and green salad.

title: Roast chicken legs with potatoes
description: Sunday tray bake: chicken legs roasted on potatoes and onions with rosemary and garlic until crisp.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the potatoes into wedges and the onions into quarters.
Toss them on a tray with the oil, garlic, rosemary and half the salt.
Rub the chicken with paprika and the rest of the salt and lay it on top, skin up.
Roast for 55 to 60 minutes until the skin is crisp and the juices run clear.
Shred the cabbage finely and dress it with vinegar, a pinch of salt and a little oil.

title: Green bean stew with pork
description: Green beans, potato and carrot simmered with small pieces of pork neck and a garlicky roux.
steps: Brown the diced pork in 1 tbsp oil. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes.
Add 1.2 litres of water and the Vegeta and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the beans, potato and carrot and cook for 20 minutes.
Make a roux with the rest of the oil, the flour, garlic and paprika, stir it in and simmer 5 minutes. Serve with a spoon of sour cream if you like.

title: Grilled squid with chard
description: Squid grilled quickly over high heat, dressed with garlic, parsley and lemon, with blitva and potatoes.
steps: Boil the cubed potatoes for 10 minutes, add the chard and cook 8 minutes more. Drain and dress with 2 tbsp oil, half the garlic and salt.
Clean the squid, pat dry, brush with oil and season.
Grill on a very hot grill pan for 2 to 3 minutes a side.
Mix the rest of the oil with the remaining garlic, parsley and lemon juice and spoon over the squid.

title: Beef goulash with polenta
description: Tender beef in a rich paprika and onion sauce, spooned over soft polenta. A cold-weather favourite.
steps: Brown the cubed beef in the oil in batches. Set aside.
Cook the chopped onions in the same pot for 15 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, grated carrot, paprika and tomato paste, then the beef, wine, bay leaves, salt, pepper and 1 litre of water.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 45 minutes until the meat is very tender.
Cook the polenta in 1.4 litres of salted water as the packet says, and serve with the goulash.

title: Potato moussaka
description: Layers of potato and seasoned minced meat baked under an egg and milk topping. Popular all over Croatia.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel and thinly slice the potatoes.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the meat, paprika, 1 tsp salt and pepper and cook until browned.
Grease a baking dish and layer potatoes and meat, starting and ending with potatoes. Sprinkle the potato layers with the rest of the salt.
Pour in 200 ml milk, cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, sour cream and remaining milk, pour over and bake uncovered for 20 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
